threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'the underground' like a proper local. And you didn't flinch when someone asked for 'jacket potatoes' at the cafe.
Last night on the 35, a bloke serenaded the entire bus with his acoustic guitar—by Tulse Hill, we were all clapping along, as if it were a proper gig.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I walked past the kiosk and saw the owner arguing passionately about the latest BVG strike gossip over his coffee. That’s when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find a late-night club hosting yoga sessions at dawn, then turning back into a full-on rave by midnight.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here if they instinctively know which BART station to avoid during a meltdown, like Civic Center right now. It’s a dance.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy singing opera on the 31-Balboa today, complete with gestures. Only in SF do you get a live performance with your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always flock to Parc Güell, but they miss the magic of Plaça del Sol at sunset—it's where we actually unwind with a vermut.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their hesitant use of 'vale'; they often overpronounce it like it’s a secret code instead of just a casual nod.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' and don’t know the 55 bus runs all night on weekends. The locals have their late-night routes down to an art.
Last night on the 37, a guy was singing Adele at the top of his lungs. The driver just laughed and joined in for a few stops!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a street musician playing a classic Turkish tune, while a couple argued over Berghain's door policy right beside him. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a mix of currywurst stands and artisan vegan cafes right next to each other, like Berlin's collision of cultures on a plate.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re local when they’ve got a favorite taco truck but can’t name a single brunch spot on Valencia.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading the crowd at the Muni stop with a ukelele, weaving through rush hour chaos. Only in SoMa do you get live music with your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think we all live on tapas and vermut. In truth, many locals are more likely to grab a bocadillo from the corner bakery on a busy day.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they line up at the wrong bus stop—locals know where to catch the express vs. the slow.
